clue.text: Peculiar clipped coins I got in football club

indicators.note: clipped means the word for coins loses its final letter

parts.note: specie is coin money, as opposed to notes

indicators.note: got in means the letter is placed inside the club's abbreviation

explanation.surface: Someone notices odd trimmed coins they have acquired at a football club.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clipped' trims the last letter from the coin word; 'got in' places I within the club abbreviation. Specie means coin money rather than notes.
explanation.definitionFit: Something peculiar to a person or place is particular to it, which is one sense of specific.

clue.text: Plant seen to be vertical earlier

parts.note: plumb means exactly vertical, as shown by a plumb line
ago means in the past, earlier

explanation.surface: A plant is observed to have stood upright before.
explanation.definitionFit: Plumbago is a flowering plant, also called leadwort, with blue or white flowers.

clue.text: Cut left-over joint?

definitions.meaning: to cut someone is to snub or ignore them
a cold cut of meat from the shoulder, left over from an earlier roast

explanation.surface: A cook slices up the meat remaining from a roast.
explanation.definitionFit: To give someone the cold shoulder is to snub them; the phrase also suggests cold roast shoulder.

clue.text: Ornamental work man heard to consent to

indicators.note: heard means the man's name is taken as it sounds, not as spelt

parts.note: Phil is a man's name, short for Philip
to agree to something is to consent to it

explanation.surface: A man is overheard agreeing to some decorative work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heard' turns PHIL into the sound FIL. This is a less common spelling of filigree.
explanation.definitionFit: Filagree is a variant of filigree, delicate ornamental work in fine gold or silver wire.

clue.text: Politician gripped by caution is the measure of a bore

indicators.note: gripped by means the politician is held inside the word for caution

parts.note: care means caution
Lib is short for Liberal, a politician

explanation.surface: A dull politician is held back by caution.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bore' suggests a tedious person, but it is the inside of a gun barrel.
explanation.definitionFit: Calibre is the internal diameter of a gun barrel, the measure of its bore.

clue.text: Letter about Tory leader is a sign of disgrace

indicators.note: about means the Greek letter goes around the other piece

parts.note: sigma is a letter of the Greek alphabet

indicators.note: leader means only the first letter of Tory is used

explanation.surface: A letter about the head of the Conservatives marks a scandal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts T, the 'leader' of Tory, inside SIGMA.
explanation.definitionFit: A stigma is a mark of shame or disgrace attached to someone.

clue.text: By no means all leavers toasted the old school

indicators.note: By no means all says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Not every school leaver drank a toast to the former school.
explanation.walkthrough: 'By no means all' picks a run from 'leavers toasted'. The Stoa was a porch in Athens that gave its name to the Stoic school.
explanation.definitionFit: The Stoics were named from the Stoa where Zeno taught, so the word stands for that ancient school of philosophy.

clue.text: Believed to be seen noisily swilling claret

indicators.note: swilling means the word holds the wine inside it like a mouthful
noisily means a word is taken as it sounds, not as spelt

parts.note: sighted means seen
claret is a red wine, so red stands for it

explanation.surface: Someone is believed to have been seen noisily gulping red wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'noisily' marks a homophone of the word for seen; 'swilling' wraps that sound round the colour of claret, as a mouth holds wine.
explanation.definitionFit: To credit a story is to believe it, so credited means believed.

clue.text: Somehow entreat a mammal to appear

indicators.note: somehow suggests the letters of the following words are arranged in some other way

explanation.surface: Someone tries to coax an animal out into the open.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Somehow' rearranges ENTREAT A into the creature.
explanation.definitionFit: The anteater is an insect-eating mammal of the Americas, so it is a specific example of the class.

clue.text: Twofold praise returned

indicators.note: returned means the word for praise is turned round and read backwards

parts.note: laud means to praise

explanation.surface: Compliments are paid back, so the praise flows both ways.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' turns LAUD round.
explanation.definitionFit: Dual means having two parts, which is what twofold describes too.

clue.text: Planning stage of project attracting the directors

parts.note: drawing a crowd means attracting it
the board is the body of directors running a company

explanation.surface: A company project gets the directors interested while it is still being planned.
explanation.definitionFit: Back to the drawing board is an idiom for returning to the planning phase of a scheme.

clue.text: No jobs? ?Select alternative that shows what one should do

definitions.text: that shows what one should do

indicators.note: alternative signals a different arrangement of the letters of No jobs and Select

explanation.surface: With no jobs, someone looks for another option as a guide to what to do.
explanation.walkthrough: 'alternative' rearranges NO JOBS SELECT.
explanation.definitionFit: An object lesson is a practical example that teaches by showing how one ought to behave.

clue.text: Turner starting to run in a sweat

parts.note: a lathe is a machine that turns wood or metal

indicators.note: starting to means only the opening letter of run is used

explanation.surface: A painter sets off at a run and is soon perspiring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turner' looks like the painter but is a machine that turns things; 'starting to' gives R from 'run'.
explanation.definitionFit: To be in a lather is to be in a sweat, flustered or agitated, as a horse foams with sweat.

clue.text: Make further changes to study in accordance with equity

parts.note: to read a subject is to study it at university
just means fair, in keeping with what is equitable

explanation.surface: A student revises their study so that it is fair to all.
explanation.walkthrough: To 'read' a subject is the British way of saying you study it at university.
explanation.definitionFit: To readjust something is to alter or adapt it again, making further changes.

clue.text: Without hesitation small rodents get into books

indicators.note: without here means outside, so the rodents surround the hesitation

parts.note: voles are small mouse-like rodents
um is the sound of someone hesitating

explanation.surface: Mice get into a library at once and chew the books.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without hesitation' reads as 'immediately', but 'Without' means outside: the rodents surround the hesitation sound.
explanation.definitionFit: A volume is a book, especially one of a set, so the plural matches books.

clue.text: Plum place where one may be stationed?

definitions.meaning: a large red dessert plum variety

definitions.text: place where one may be stationed?
definitions.meaning: a London railway terminus, where travellers wait at the station

explanation.surface: A plum is found at the place where someone is posted.
explanation.walkthrough: Victoria is a London mainline station; 'stationed' is a pun on posting.
explanation.definitionFit: The Victoria is a well-known variety of plum, and Victoria Station is a London rail terminus.

clue.text: Beloved of Eros died frightened

parts.note: in Greek myth Psyche was loved by Eros, the god of love
d is the abbreviation for died, as in family trees

explanation.surface: The god of love's sweetheart died of fright.
explanation.definitionFit: To be psyched out is to be unnerved, so the word can mean frightened or intimidated.

clue.text: To avoid ominous date in March, walk outside

indicators.note: outside means the word for walk goes around the date

parts.note: a step is a pace in walking
the Ides of March, 15 March, was the day Caesar was warned of

explanation.surface: To dodge the fateful March date, someone goes for a walk outdoors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outside' wraps the walk word round the date. The Ides of March is the date Julius Caesar was warned about and killed.
explanation.definitionFit: To sidestep a problem is to avoid or evade it.

clue.text: Exorbitant demand is without force

parts.note: ex means without, as in ex dividend
action is force or effort exerted

explanation.surface: An unreasonable claim is said to lack any power.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like a container word but gives EX, as in 'ex dividend'.
explanation.definitionFit: An exaction is the act of demanding, especially an excessive levy or payment.

clue.text: Show interest and use the new building

indicators.note: building means the letters are put together in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Someone shows interest and makes use of the newly built premises.
explanation.walkthrough: 'building' rearranges USE THE with N, from 'new'.
explanation.definitionFit: To enthuse is to show eager interest or excitement about something.

clue.text: Knitted jacket: for a corgi

definitions.meaning: a woollen jacket that buttons down the front
the ... Welsh corgi is one of the two breeds of corgi

explanation.surface: Someone is knitting a little coat for their dog.
explanation.walkthrough: The corgi breeds are the Pembroke and the Cardigan, named after Welsh counties.
explanation.definitionFit: The garment is named after the Earl of Cardigan, and the dog breed after the Welsh county.

clue.text: Boyish girl popular in sport

indicators.note: in means the word for popular goes inside the word for sport

parts.note: a game is a sport
in means fashionable or popular

explanation.surface: A tomboy is popular in sporting circles.
explanation.definitionFit: A gamine is a slim girl with a boyish, mischievous charm.

clue.text: Everything can be found in the German city

indicators.note: can be found in means the word for everything sits inside the German article

parts.note: das is a German word for the
all means everything

explanation.surface: Everything you could want is found in the German city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can be found in' wraps the German article round the word for everything. 'German' tempts one towards a German city; the city is in Texas.
explanation.definitionFit: Dallas is a large city in the US state of Texas.

clue.text: Too much stress unravelling as he improves

indicators.note: unravelling means the letters of as he improves come apart and are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone getting better finds the pressure is too much and comes apart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unravelling' rearranges AS HE IMPROVES.
explanation.definitionFit: Overemphasis is excessive stress laid on something, giving it too much weight.

clue.text: Invented a cheese?

parts.note: read backwards, the name of a Dutch cheese spells a word meaning invented

explanation.surface: Someone claims to have created a new cheese.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark hints that the cheese's name, reversed, gives a word for invented.
explanation.definitionFit: Edam is a mild Dutch cheese whose letters reversed spell a synonym for created.

clue.text: Flash fellow makes people who matter recoil

indicators.note: recoil means the abbreviation for important people springs back and reads backwards

parts.note: VIPs are very important people

explanation.surface: A showy man makes the important people shrink back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recoil' turns VIPS round. A spiv is a British term for a flashy petty crook.
explanation.definitionFit: A spiv is a flashily dressed man who lives by sharp dealing, so he is a flash fellow.

clue.text: Idols are gripping in' pictures

indicators.note: gripping means the word for idols holds the little word in inside it

parts.note: images are idols, as in graven images

explanation.surface: Idols appear gripping on film or in pictures.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gripping' holds the little word inside the idols word. 'pictures' looks like a noun but is a verb: to picture is to imagine.
explanation.definitionFit: To picture something is to form a mental image of it, so pictures means imagines.

clue.text: Interpreter using index

definitions.meaning: someone who explains or performs a work, as a leading performer of an art
in mathematics an index is the power to which a number is raised

explanation.surface: A translator works by using an index.
explanation.definitionFit: An exponent is someone who interprets or performs, and in maths an index or power.
